From a8d51efb5929ae308895455a3e496b5eca2cd143 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Youngjun Park <youngjun.park@lge.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 21:05:28 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] PM: sleep: Drop spurious WARN_ON() from pm_restore_gfp_mask()

Commit 35e4a69b2003f ("PM: sleep: Allow pm_restrict_gfp_mask()
stacking") introduced refcount-based GFP mask management that warns
when pm_restore_gfp_mask() is called with saved_gfp_count == 0.

Some hibernation paths call pm_restore_gfp_mask() defensively where
the GFP mask may or may not be restricted depending on the execution
path. For example, the uswsusp interface invokes it in
SNAPSHOT_CREATE_IMAGE, SNAPSHOT_UNFREEZE, and snapshot_release().
Before the stacking change this was a silent no-op; it now triggers
a spurious WARNING.

Remove the WARN_ON() wrapper from the !saved_gfp_count check while
retaining the check itself, so that defensive calls remain harmless
without producing false warnings.

Fixes: 35e4a69b2003f ("PM: sleep: Allow pm_restrict_gfp_mask() stacking")
Signed-off-by: Youngjun Park <youngjun.park@lge.com>
[ rjw: Subject tweak ]
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260322120528.750178-1-youngjun.park@lge.com
Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>

diff --git a/kernel/power/main.c b/kernel/power/main.c
index 5f8c9e12eaec..5429e9f19b65 100644
--- a/kernel/power/main.c
+++ b/kernel/power/main.c
@@ -40,7 +40,7 @@ void pm_restore_gfp_mask(void)
 {
 	WARN_ON(!mutex_is_locked(&system_transition_mutex));
 
-	if (WARN_ON(!saved_gfp_count) || --saved_gfp_count)
+	if (!saved_gfp_count || --saved_gfp_count)
 		return;
 
 	gfp_allowed_mask = saved_gfp_mask;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of modifications

### 1. Modifications in each file

**`kernel/power/main.c`**:  
- Line 43: Changed `if (WARN_ON(!saved_gfp_count) || --saved_gfp_count)` to `if (!saved_gfp_count || --saved_gfp_count)`.  
  - Removed the `WARN_ON()` macro from the check that tests whether `saved_gfp_count` is zero.  
  - The underlying condition (`!saved_gfp_count || --saved_gfp_count`) is preserved, so the function still returns early without restoring the GFP mask when the count is zero.

### 2. Relationship of modifications

The change is contained entirely within one file and affects a single logical branch in `pm_restore_gfp_mask()`. The previous commit (35e4a69b2003f) added the `WARN_ON` to catch unexpected mismatches in the refcount-based GFP mask management. However, certain hibernation code paths (e.g., via the uswsusp interface) call `pm_restore_gfp_mask()` defensively even when no prior restriction was applied, causing false positive warnings. By removing the `WARN_ON` while keeping the guard condition, the patch prevents those spurious warnings while maintaining the correct behavior (the call becomes a harmless no-op when no restriction is active). This ensures that defensive callers remain safe without triggering unnecessary kernel warnings.

PM: sleep: Drop spurious WARN_ON() from pm_restore_gfp_mask()

Commit 35e4a69b2003f ("PM: sleep: Allow pm_restrict_gfp_mask()
stacking") introduced refcount-based GFP mask management that warns
when pm_restore_gfp_mask() is called with saved_gfp_count == 0.

the GFP mask may or may not be restricted depending on the execution
path. For example, the uswsusp interface invokes it in
SNAPSHOT_CREATE_IMAGE, SNAPSHOT_UNFREEZE, and snapshot_release().
Before the stacking change this was a silent no-op; it now triggers
a spurious WARNING.

Remove the WARN_ON() wrapper from the !saved_gfp_count check while

without producing false warnings.

Fixes: 35e4a69b2003f ("PM: sleep: Allow pm_restrict_gfp_mask() stacking")
Signed-off-by: Youngjun Park <youngjun.park@lge.com>
[ rjw: Subject tweak ]

Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>

Here is the root cause:
After commit 35e4a69b2003f introduced refcount-based GFP mask management, pm_restore_gfp_mask() added a WARN_ON to catch calls when saved_gfp_count is zero. However, some hibernation code paths (e.g., uswsusp) defensively call pm_restore_gfp_mask() even if no prior restriction occurred, triggering the WARN_ON unnecessarily. The fix removes the WARN_ON while keeping the guard condition.

Here is the patch:
 
 void pm_restore_gfp_mask(void)
 {
 	WARN_ON(!mutex_is_locked(&system_transition_mutex));
 
-	if (WARN_ON(!saved_gfp_count) || --saved_gfp_count)
+	if (!saved_gfp_count || --saved_gfp_count)
 		return;
 
 	gfp_allowed_mask = saved_gfp_mask;
 	saved_gfp_mask = 0;
 
 	pm_pr_dbg("GFP mask restored\n");
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```
if (WARN_ON(!saved_gfp_count) || --saved_gfp_count)
```
Reason:
This line in `pm_restore_gfp_mask()` triggers a `WARN_ON` when `saved_gfp_count` is zero. Defensive calls (e.g., from uswsusp paths like `SNAPSHOT_CREATE_IMAGE`, `SNAPSHOT_UNFREEZE`, `snapshot_release()` that may not have previously restricted the GFP mask) cause this warning to fire spuriously, as the commit 35e4a69b2003f added the warning without accounting for such defensive invocations.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```
if (!saved_gfp_count || --saved_gfp_count)
```
Reason:
This replacement removes the `WARN_ON()` wrapper while keeping the original logical check (`!saved_gfp_count`). It ensures that when `saved_gfp_count` is zero (due to a defensive call with no prior restriction), the function returns early without printing a false warning. The refcount-based protection against underflow is retained because the early return still prevents decrementing below zero.
